title: Recursive type stack zoom loop
summary: A two-word lockup repeated as a shrinking column of copies on black; the front copy zooms up and out of frame while the next one grows into its place, so one second loops without a seam.
use_when: A seamless loop for a social post, story sticker or website hero
An intro or outro sting built from a two-word name or slogan
A type-only background behind a talk, stream or event screen
Hypnotic filler between scenes of a longer film

look.type_style: heavy geometric sans, italic, lowercase, tight leading (lines overlap by ~10 %), front lockup ~45 % of frame width at f0, copies below at ~0.4x each step

sfx.event: front copy flies out past the frame (once per loop, ~f10-f18)

structure.shot: two-word lockup, white on black, repeated ~8 times in a column that shrinks and tightens downward; copies overlap; front copy zooms past
structure.camera: static frame; the stack itself scales: front copy ~0.80 -> ~6+ frame widths in 30 fr, rising ~83 px/s @1920 (motion.json zoom 117 %/s)
structure.motion: every copy takes the place of the one above in 30 fr; scale rides easings.inExpo-like acceleration (widths in strip: f0 0.79, f5 0.92, f11 1.5+, f17 off-frame); next copy settles easings.outQuint into f0 size by f29; self-similar so f29 = f0

params.brand: any brand.json: display font (heavy, ideally italic), fg for the type, bg
params.content.lines: two short words or a two-line name, one word per line, <= 8 letters each
params.copies: number of copies in the column (default 8)
params.ratio: scale of each copy relative to the one above (default ~0.42)
params.timing.period: frames per loop at 30 fps (default 30 = 1 s), scaled to fps
params.aspect: 1:1 | 4:5 | 9:16 | 16:9; the column stays centred, front copy ~80 % of width at f0

notes: Measured from a 30 fps strip (1 fr resolution, scale estimates from widths at 320 px, about +-3 %): front lockup width 0.79 of frame at f0, 0.92 at f5, exceeds the frame by f8, only giant fragments of it remain f12-f19; second copy reaches f0 size at f29, so the loop wraps seamlessly at 30 fr. Copies are drawn as a union of white fills (no outline, no shadow), each overlapping the next by ~25 % of its height; the column tapers to small copies near the bottom third. No camera move or cut: the zoom is in the content. Proposed term 'recursive-zoom' (not in vocabulary, not used as an id). sfx planned by the glue rule, not measured (source is silent).
